output.name: Hatun — The Bailing Gourd (The Leeward Reach)
output.myth: When Aun cut the string, the sky went off up the wind and left the boats below to the Gale. Hatun was out with her two children when Tavo came down laughing and filled the hull. She did not pray. She bailed with the gourd she used for broth until her wrists were bark and the children lay quiet. Tavo laughed and blew harder. Hesk, who keeps count at the pole, counted every scoop. At dawn the boat was still afloat, though Hatun was not. Ennu sewed her into sailcloth and hung her gourd beside her, so something would keep bailing the dark. East of her, Tirun lies keel-up with its lamps burning after the oil should be gone; the old women say that is Hatun's work. Far south, Varo's grey boatman takes his shell coin from the drowned, but Hatun had only a gourd, and she is still paying with it. Look for her low in the south. Each drop off the lip is one she would not let go down. Keep your scoop by the door. Tavo does not forgive, but he does get bored.
output.finding: Start at Tirun, the Upturned Hull, low in the south, and go a fist and a half (about 14°) straight west along the sky to find Hatun's gourd.
